start_here_runtime: 57 minutes with the full response; 55–60 with normal variation. The manuscript is 6,874 words at about 120 words per minute.
start_here_cut: If you have 50 minutes: Introduction to 4, Movement 1 to 6, Movement 2 to 6, Movement 4 to 6, Application to 6. Keep the sign/source distinction, “he did not know,” the prayer in the temple, and the risen temple.
start_here_guardrails: Do not celebrate Samson’s final act. It is a suicide-adjacent act of revenge; preach it as tragedy and grace, and provide crisis-care language.
Do not make Delilah the sole villain. The text focuses on Samson’s choices, and she is not labeled a prostitute.
Keep the history honest: the hair is the sign, the Spirit is the source; the Gaza temple is not archaeologically identified.
Do not preach Judges 16:20 as loss of salvation; it is the withdrawal of the Spirit’s empowerment for Samson’s calling.
Do not turn Samson into a simple Christ figure. The connection is contrast, not allegory.
start_here_evidence: The Nazirite vow, the Spirit’s empowerment, the Gaza prison, and the Dagon temple are doing theological work, and the empty tomb is the turn.

slides.run: A SERMON FOR THE PULPIT · 55–60 MINUTES

slides.label: 01 · THE BIG IDEA
slides.note: Strength was never the point. The source was.

slides.label: 02 · THE GIFT
slides.headline: Set apart before he was born.
slides.kicker: The sign is not the source.

slides.label: 04 · THE PRICE
slides.headline: A secret with a price tag.
slides.body: The Philistines did not want Samson dead. They wanted to know where his strength came from. The price was not for his head. It was for his secret.
slides.pullquote: They did not want his head. They wanted his secret.
slides.footline: The secret was never in his hair. It was in the LORD.

slides.label: 05 · THE NIGHT
slides.headline: He did not know.
slides.quote: “I will go out as at other times and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the LORD had left him.
slides.aside1: The old motions. The old assumption.
slides.aside2: He reached for the strength and found only his own arm. The source had gone.
slides.footline: The most dangerous sentence in the story: “as at other times.”

slides.label: 06 · THE COLLAPSE
slides.footline: He killed more in his death than in his life. It is a body count, not a trophy.

slides.label: 07 · THE GOSPEL
slides.banner_main: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
lines: Samson pulled down the house and died.
Jesus let his body be pulled down and rose.
slides.footline: Samson is what we are. Jesus is what we need.

slides.label: 08 · THE TRUE TEMPLE
slides.banner_main: “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.”
lines: The gospel does not recruit heroes.
slides.footline: The strongest man died blind. The Son of God went into the dark and came out alive.

slides.label: 09 · THE RESPONSE
slides.headline: What do you do with the strength?

title: Name the gift,
not the muscle.
items.desc: The Spirit was the source. Your strength is a gift to steward, not a self to worship.

title: Do not confuse
the sign.
items.desc: Ministry, knowledge, and reputation are good. They are not the source.

title: Tell the truth
about your eyes.
items.desc: You cannot see your own blind spots alone. Let someone close tell you the truth.

title: Pray the
small prayer.
items.desc: “Remember me” is enough. The thief on the cross prayed it too.

slides.footline: The sign is not the source. The routine is not the relationship.

slides.label: 10 · THE INVITATION
slides.line1: Not stronger. Not cleaner. Not with a plan. Just honest.

slides.kicker: SILENCED SAINTS · PREACH THE FORGOTTEN · SERMON KIT 4
slides.line2: The Son of God went in for him.
slides.body: He came out alive. He is still calling people out of the dark.
